in_text_mentions: Concerning the thorax, the primary abnormality concerns the ribs, which can be “paddle-shaped” or “oar-shaped” (Figure 2). Modifications of the shape of vertebral bodies was saw in all patients, resulting in flattened and rounded vertebrae (Figure 3). At the thoraco-lumbar level, the vertebral body can show a deficiency in its anterosuperior corner and, consequently, an apparent prolongation of the anteroinferior one, resulting in the lateral X-ray in an “anterior beaking” aspect. When hypoplasia of both anterior corners occurs, the vertebral body is wedge-shaped.
